messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] P95 token latency spike on prod inference cluster (region: us-west-2). Severity: P2. Triggered by metric: inference.token_latency.p95 > 1200ms for 5m. Pager routed to #eng-oncall and oncall rotation.

oncall-rotation: Paging sara for primary, mike for backup. Sara, you on? :bell: @sara

sara: I’m up. looking at traces and LC. First quick check: are there any recent deploys?

mike: Not that I'm aware of, no deploys in the last 30m. I can pull logs if you want.

sara: grabbing p95 dashboard now. seeing a couple noisy hosts with 2-3s spikes. Suspect a bad batch of large-context requests spiking KV cache misses.

raj: FYI customer support reported slow responses for a few enterprise tenants ~10:45 PT. Could be related.

luis: which model pool is this hitting? I see increased queue length for pool-roberta-1 and pool-gptx-2.

kayla: tagging product 14 some canary traffic had longer contexts earlier today, maybe correlated.

sara: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily increase routing to region fallback (eu-west) for non-enterprise tier; 2) enable per-route prefix caching bypass for suspect tenant(s); 3) scale up pool-roberta-1 by 2 nodes. I'll start 1 and 3.

mike: I'll open a ticket for customer impact (CS-12345) and annotate affected tenants. raj can you paste the support logs?

raj: pasted support excerpt: "Customers reporting timeouts and partial responses, 10% failure rate between 10:42-10:53". Added to CS-12345.

incident-bot: Action taken: scaled pool-roberta-1 +2 nodes at 1940000150. Routing adjustment applied: non-enterprise -> eu-west fallback at 1940000153.

sara: after scale and fallback, p95 dropped from ~1400ms -> ~650ms over 3 minutes. Queue length normalized. Still seeing a tail on a couple machines.

mike: I dug through instance logs: repeated KV cache eviction errors on host gpu-22 (OOM while merging kv). File attached: /var/log/inference/kv-merge.err (link).

luis: ok that's a hardware-specific failure pattern. We should cordon gpu-22 and drain.

kayla: can we avoid paging on similar alerts for single-host kv errors? This causes noisy pages; maybe downgrade severity if host_count < 2 and overall p95 < 1.2s?

sara: Agree. Post-incident action: tune alerting rule for inference.token_latency.p95 to only page when (p95 > 1200ms AND affected_host_count >= 2) OR (p95 > 2000ms). For single-host spikes under 2s -> create ticket only.

mike: Also recommend a new dashboard tile that shows affected_host_count, KV eviction rate, and per-pool queue length together. I can make a draft.

raj: CS updated with mitigation summary and timeline. No enterprise SLA breaches detected (we rerouted enterprise traffic to dedicated pools early).

incident-bot: Host gpu-22 cordoned at 1940000165. Drain started.

sara: Handoff note for next oncall (mike): remaining work 14 (1) confirm gpu-22 drain completes and replace hardware; (2) implement alert rule tweak in staging and run chaos test; (3) create dashboard PR with tiles Mike proposed; (4) follow up with platform team about KV memory growth patterns.

mike: taking handoff. I'll file the three follow-ups as cards in board: INF-3487 (alert rule tuning), INF-3488 (dashboard for alert correlation), INF-3489 (hardware remediation gpu-22).

kayla: quick policy suggestion: change routing/escalation mapping so host-isolated infra incidents (single-host OOMs, kernel panics) do NOT immediately page eng-oncall; instead, route to #eng-infra and create ticket for eng-oncall if host_count >=2 or service-level impact detected. This will reduce page noise.

luis: +1. We should keep an exception for customer-visible timeouts where error_rate > 1% and latency > 1.5s 14 still page.

sara: agreed. I'll draft a short RFC for the alert-routing and severity policy change: page vs ticket rules, escalation windows, channel mappings (#eng-infra vs #eng-oncall vs #incidents). Aim to have RFC out EOD tomorrow.

mike: also propose adding a new alert label "page_criteria" that documents which criteria must be met to escalate. That will make future rule changes easier to audit.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: token latency p95 back to baseline at 1940000178. Summary: root cause suspected KV merge OOM on gpu-22; mitigated by scaling pool and routing fallback. Severity downgraded to P3.

sara: closing thread with action items. Will follow up RFC + alert tests. Thanks all. :coffee:

mike: noted. I'll take INF-3488 and start the dashboard draft.

oncall-rotation: thanks team, marking incident as handled and updating oncall calendar.
